title: Autotune safety layer for customer batch/cache profiles
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description:
Goal: Build an automated suggestion and safe-apply service that proposes per-customer and per-route batching and KV caching profiles, validates them via simulation and telemetry, and applies them using staged rollouts with automatic rollback on regressions. The service should support segmentation (route / customer / customer-tier), allowlists/denylists for policy exemptions, and explicit tier-based controls for Dedicated vs Hosted customers.

Background: We already have runtime hooks for batching and KV cache. Manual tuning has delivered wins but does not scale. Previous efforts (ENG-40211, ENG-34108) provided policy primitives and per-route presets. This ticket implements the safety and orchestration layer to move from recommendations to automated, reversible changes while protecting SLAs and customer-critical traffic.
acceptance_criteria: Suggestion engine produces per-customer and per-route candidate profiles with estimated delta in token-cost and p95 latency within 5% of observed when simulated.
Dry-run simulator can replay 7 days of production traces and produce a safety report (errors, latency changes, cache hit delta) for a candidate profile.
Safe-apply pipeline supports canary -> ramp -> full rollout with automatic rollback triggered by pre-defined SLO breach rules or quality regressions.
Support segmentation rules: allowlist/denylist override and tier-scoped defaults. Admin UI and API for whitelist/blacklist entries exists.
All applied changes are logged to audit trail with rollback reason and associated telemetry links.
No customer-facing incidents caused during canaries across 3 pilot customers (tiered: free, standard, enterprise).
technical_notes:
Architecture: suggestion_service (heuristic + ML scoring) -> simulator (trace-based dry-run) -> policy_guard (segmentation, allow/deny rules, tier limits) -> orchestrator (canary/ramp automation) -> apply_agent (runtime API).

Suggestion model: start with rule-based heuristics (prefix hotness, avg tokens per request, p50/p95 latency margin) and a lightweight gradient-boosted regressor to predict cost/latency delta. Keep model explainability for operator trust.

Simulator: record-based replay using production sampling stored in logstore. Simulator must model batching behaviour (batch window variability) and KV cache warm/cold startup effects.

Safety checks: SLO thresholds (p95 latency, error rate), quality checks (lossy decoding divergence on sampled prompts), and cost guardrails (max allowed cost change per customer per week).

Rollback: automatic if SLO breach detected during canary/ramp; manual rollback button for operators; immediate freeze if a high-severity signal is observed.

Data retention: keep dry-run traces and reports for 90 days. Ensure PII is stripped before simulations for regulated customers.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal dev experiment + unit tests (teams: runtime, telemetry) - complete
Phase 1: simulator validation using 14 days of anonymized traces - target 2026-03-05
Phase 2: 3 pilot customers (one per tier) with manual approval -> canary automation for non-critical routes
Phase 3: enable auto-rollout for low-risk routes with tight guardrails
Phase 4: expand to all eligible routes and expose admin controls in Console for allowlist/denylist and tier overrides
test_plan: Unit tests for suggestion heuristics and model scoring
Integration tests: simulator vs runtime with synthetic traces to validate p95 predictions
E2E canary test: apply change to opt-in test tenant and verify rollback triggers under injected latency/error
Security review for trace anonymization and KMS usage
Load test for orchestrator to ensure it can manage 1k concurrent rollouts
risks: False positives in suggestion engine could recommend aggressive batching that increases p95 latency for tail customers
Simulator fidelity gap: replay may not capture transient infra bottlenecks leading to missed regressions
Operator confusion over allowlist/denylist precedence if not surfaced clearly in Console
Potential data leakage if traces are not properly scrubbed before simulation
